front: Average-case time to insert into a BST?
What input order produces a degenerate (worst-case) BST?
back: Already-sorted input — the tree becomes a linked list, O(n) operations.

front: In-order traversal of a BST visits nodes in what order?
back: Ascending sorted order of their values.

front: BST delete: a node with two children is removed by replacing it with...?
back: Its successor — the smallest key in its right subtree (found by walking left from z.right until there's no more left child).

front: Preorder traversal alone — does it uniquely determine a tree's shape?
back: No. But preorder + inorder together (with all-unique keys) do uniquely reconstruct the tree.

front: Which traversal order is naturally suited to safely deleting an entire tree?
back: Postorder (left, right, node) — children are freed before their parent.

front: What is the BST invariant for a node z?
back: Everything in z's left subtree is < z.key, everything in z's right subtree is ≥ z.key.
